text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Referral to clinical psychology for a trauma-informed diagnostic evaluation of nightmares, watchfulness, and short sleep, with trauma-focused psychotherapy (cognitive processing therapy or prolonged exposure) offered if he meets criteria for PTSD and wants it
  • Trauma-informed care at every visit: explain each question, examination, and test before it happens and ask his agreement; offer a chaperone; let him choose what to share and stop at any time; no retelling of details is needed for his care
  • Measurement-based follow-up: PCL-5 and PHQ-9 at each chronic-care visit and hand pain on a 0 to 10 scale at every visit
  • Hand care: diclofenac 1% gel up to four times a day; six sessions with a hand therapist over eight weeks for range-of-motion and strengthening exercises and joint protection; a wide-barrel pen, a ten-minute break each hour of writing, and dictation for long drafts
  • A care plan built on the strengths he names: his work and writing, his family and community, and his faith, with visits scheduled around his travel for speaking
  • Brief behavioral treatment for insomnia in two sessions with Dr. Morrison: a fixed waking time, a seven-hour sleep window, no writing in the last hour before bed, a short routine for nights after a nightmare, and a two-week sleep diary

resource.title: Frederick Douglass synthetic care plan
resource.description: Trauma-informed primary care for a 34-year-old editor, author, and public speaker who survived violence, hunger and cold, and separation from his mother in childhood and youth, and assaults in adulthood: consent at each step and his choice of what to share; the PC-PTSD-5 and PCL-5 read against their cut-points; a structured diagnostic interview by clinical psychology that finds trauma-related symptoms below the threshold for post-traumatic stress disorder, so no PTSD diagnosis is made and trauma-focused psychotherapy (cognitive processing therapy or prolonged exposure) and medication (sertraline, paroxetine, or venlafaxine) are kept in reserve for if PTSD develops and he wants them, under the VA/DoD 2023 guideline; brief behavioral treatment for short sleep and occasional nightmares; post-traumatic osteoarthritis of the right hand after fractures that were not set, treated with topical diclofenac, hand therapy, and writing adaptations under the ACR 2019 guideline and the CMID; measurement-based follow-up with the PCL-5, PHQ-9, and hand-pain score, including an honest record of a missed hand-function measure; and a plan built on the strengths he names: his work, his writing, his family and community, and his faith.
